      <title>Five EU states announce plans for immigration ‘return hubs’ in Rwanda</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/eu-states-immigration-return-hubs-rwanda</link>
      <description><p>Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark and Greece likely to face challenges to policy criticised as ‘grave moral failing’</p><p>Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and has been denounced as “a grave moral failing”.</p><p>The five countries – Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece – are the first to seek to use the EU’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/mar/26/meps-back-plans-for-return-hubs-raising-fears-of-human-rights-black-holes">newly agreed returns law</a> that allows<em> </em>people who have exhausted all avenues of appeal against their removal from Europe to be sent to a third country.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/eu-states-immigration-return-hubs-rwanda">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <media:content width="140" url="https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/d668e44ea9f6f3fb2d88cfee76bb772cccada10f/456_0_4053_3243/master/4053.jpg?width=140&quality=85&auto=format&fit=max&s=7839a06430930a2378822738556852d7">

News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 16:04:24 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category></category><title>Serbia's student-backed MPs take seats in parliament after election win</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261117-serbia-s-student-backed-mps-take-seats-in-parliament-after-election-win</link><description>
Serbia's Student ⁠List lawmakers entered parliament ​on Tuesday, cheered on by hundreds of supporters, after their October ​election victory ended 14 years of rule by the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS). The Student List, a group that includes academics, professionals, farmers, actors and activists ​chosen ‌by student assemblies, secured 140 seats in the ⁠250-member parliament in October 25 polls, while the SNS gained 104.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/87a472fc-e29d-11f1-b8c8-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261117-162342-162539-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/87a472fc-e29d-11f1-b8c8-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261117-162342-162539-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">8cdbfc0e-e29d-11f1-bae2-1546e6274c7a</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 15:48:34 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Americas</category><title>Trump says he takes possible Iran bomb threat to Washington 'very seriously'</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20261117-trump-says-he-takes-possible-iran-bomb-threat-to-washington-very-seriously</link><description>
President Donald Trump said Tuesday that US authorities take any possible threats to Washington ‘very seriously’, following reports that Iran was planning to target senior Trump administration officials, possibly with a radioactive bomb.  Tehran dismissed the reports as ‘fabricated’.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/33aa0a04-e298-11f1-ba28-1ba7ddfab527/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26321504671499.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/33aa0a04-e298-11f1-ba28-1ba7ddfab527/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26321504671499.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">44b532ae-e29a-11f1-9632-a7bb1405c60d</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 15:44:54 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/33aa0a04-e298-11f1-ba28-1ba7ddfab527/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26321504671499.jpg">©  Aaron Favila, Pool AP via AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>arts24</category><title>Urban Zulu and '100 Reasons to Stay Single in Lagos': Telling African stories on their own terms</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/arts24/20261117-urban-zulu-and-100-reasons-to-stay-single-in-lagos-telling-african-stories-on-their-own-terms</link><description>
Africa's creative industries are attracting growing international attention, from fashion and film to television and music. But as African stories reach audiences around the world, a bigger question is emerging: who gets to tell those stories, and who gets to shape how the continent is seen? At FAME Week Africa in Cape Town, arts24 met some of the creatives driving that conversation.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/5aed8f1a-e292-11f1-ad9e-ff16da94d1fe/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-d40612db.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/5aed8f1a-e292-11f1-ad9e-ff16da94d1fe/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-d40612db.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">63b88830-e291-11f1-88b7-b140e2808fcf</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 15:44:37 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Eve JACKSON</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>France's Le Pen promises to lower retirement age if she wins election</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261117-france-s-le-pen-promises-to-lower-retirement-age-if-she-wins-election</link><description>
French far-right ​leader Marine Le ​Pen vowed on Tuesday to repeal President ​Emmanuel ‌Macron's pension ⁠reform if she is ‌elected next spring and ⁠bring down the retirement age to ​60 to 62. She ‌also set out plans to ‌create a fund worth €900 ​billion ($990.54 billion) to help pay for pensions in ​the long term. It ​would take a generation ​to build up the fund, she added.

Astronauts get tasked with all kinds of weird science aboard the International Space Station. Recently, NASA astronaut and Crew-13 commander Jessica Watkins got to work supporting an ongoing experiment that includes 3D-printing human cells and tissues in space.

What is it?

Aboard the space station, astronauts have a multitude of responsibilities ranging from station maintenance and repairs on spacewalks to daily exercise and a wide variety of scientific research.

Watkins recently shared a snapshot captured by her crewmate Anil Menon that showcases her experience working on an experiment called InSPA-Auxilium Bioprinter-Cell Printing that takes place inside the station's Life Sciences Glovebox, a contained research space and one of Watkins favorite places to work on the space station, she shared on social media.

In the image she is gloved-up with both her hands and arms covered in the sealed glovebox while she mixes samples of living cells with a bioink, a mixture she then inserts into a specialized cartridge, NASA shared.

Why is it incredible?

This experiment that Watkins is working on "leverages the microgravity environment of ISS to 3D print cells and manufacture human liver, kidney, and cartilage tissue. Just one of many examples of how we’re using this amazing orbital national laboratory to reshape our understanding of biology, medicine, and engineering, and improve life on Earth!" Watkins shared online.

This experiment is designed to explore 3D printing human cartilage tissue in microgravity. The experiment aims to one day support future human patients both in space and on Earth.

When you think of the research that happens in space, 3D-printing human cells might not be the first thing to come to mind. But because of the unique microgravity environment onboard the ISS, it is the perfect home for even the strangest of biological experiments.

On the space station, there is still gravity but objects (and people) remain in a sort of constant freefall, leading to total weightlessness that mimics the complete absence of gravity. This weightlessness allows researchers to test, experiment and explore beyond the gravitational confines of Earth.

At the peak of the shower, observers at Kitt Peak National Observatory in Arizona estimated an astonishing 40 meteors per second streaking across the sky. That's 2,400 shooting stars per minute, or a staggering 144,000 per hour. It was a spectacle that many regard as the greatest meteor display in recorded history.

It's hard to imagine what it was like to experience such a spectacle. But who better to tell us than those who saw it with their own eyes? To mark the 60th anniversary of the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966, we asked those who saw it to share their memories.

'One of the most loved and memorable nights of my life'

"I was around 9 years old at the time of the 1966 Leonid storm, living a few miles east of Roxie, Mississippi. We lived in a rural, dark, relatively remote area with almost zero outside lights.

"I and a couple cousins were spending the night at our Uncle and Aunt's house, staying up late, just fooling around outside like young kids do when living in the 'sticks'. As we walked down a road, I remember hearing an almost constant series of little whistling, zipping sounds. The sounds were similar to when you light a nylon rope on fire and as it burns, little flaming droplets drip down with a zippy sound.

"I looked up and the sky was filled with streaks of 'shooting stars' and I realized that was what made the sounds. I yelled at my cousins to look up and we could hardly believe what we saw. We all laid down on our backs and for a couple of hours just watched and listened to what seemed like 1000's of 'shooting stars' zipping and zinging overhead. I could even smell the sulphur-like odor from the burning little bits of space dust.

"I'm nearly 70 years old now but I'll never forget that experience. I always knew what I'd seen that night was special but not until much later in life, after the internet, did I realize just how lucky I was to have experienced that storm. That night was one of the most loved and memorable nights of my life and I'll treasure it forever."

'Students and faculty were pounding on doors to get people, including neighbors, to watch'

"I was an astronomy lab assistant at Southwestern College in Winfield, KS, in 1966, majoring in physics and math and the physics professor was sure that the Leonids would be an amazing shower worth the class time.

"The sky was clear. He called me early the morning of the 17th and told me to get to the campus. I can't remember the exact time as students and faculty were pounding on doors to get people, including neighbors,to watch.

"We were all lying in an open grassy area because that was the best way to see the whole sky. It was like a humongous fireworks display and lasted even as the sun began to rise.

"As years have gone by, I have felt grateful and privileged to have seen such a wonderful astronomical event."

'It looked like every star in the sky was falling'

"I was 18 and spent the night in El Paso, Texas, lying on the ground in my backyard and watching. It looked like every star in the sky was falling. It was amazing!"

'We watched them all night'

"I was 9 years old and was camping with my dad in the western mountains of California. We were set up to sleep outside, but on this particular night, we saw more meteors than I have ever seen before or since. We watched them all night and didn't get much sleep."

'It took your breath away'

"Brooklyn Center, Minnesota. 14 years old. Watched in our front yard. The sky was full. It took your breath away"

'I assumed they would all be as interesting'

"I was 3 years old at the time of the 1966 Leonid meteor shower. I remember very little at that age, but watching the sky fall that night was seared in my memory.

"My family was living in Troy, Alabama, at the time. My father, a professor of psychology, was a man of science with a special love of astronomy, which he passed onto his young son.

"He drove us several miles out of town until the skies were dark, without interference from the lights of the town. Troy was much smaller then and it was easy to find dark, clear skies.

"I remember that it was a little chilly that night. My father and I stretched out on the hood of the car, the warmth of the engine radiating against our backs.

"That night was my first meteor shower, and only many years later did I learn that year's Leonids were historic. Sadly, though I bore witness to the display, we missed the true event by several hours as I grew tired by 1:00 AM, and my father had to teach class in the morning.

"I remember many bright, colorful, and long-trailed meteors. Some left 'tails' that hung in the sky for several seconds. We only experienced the beginning of the event, but it is a core memory with my father.

"That night/morning spoiled me for future meteor watches; I assumed they would all be as interesting."

'I guess the party is over'

Not everyone was lucky enough to witness the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966. For some, the night was memorable for an entirely different reason.

Space.com columnist Joe Rao was just 10 years old at the time, and despite eagerly anticipating the display, the weather had other ideas.

"Standing in my backyard late on a Wednesday night in the Throggs Neck section of The Bronx, cursing the heavens. My grandfather stood at my side, just shaking his head and murmuring two words over and over: 'Too bad.'

"Clouds covered the midnight sky like a fresh coat of plaster, smearing my view of the Leonids. My mom, sister and grandmother, as well as my neighbors had long since trudged to bed, leaving only Grandpa and I to gaze at a charcoal gray sky totally devoid of stars."

Rao had been looking forward to the storm ever since a visit to New York's Hayden Planetarium, where astronomer Fred C. Hess had encouraged visitors to look out for what could be a spectacular display.

But when Rao and his grandfather ventured outside, there wasn't a single star in sight.

"After a few minutes, I sobbed to my grandfather, 'But they promised it was only going to be partly cloudy tonight.' To which he sadly replied, 'I guess the party is over.'"

What caused the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966?

The Leonid meteor shower occurs every November when Earth passes through a stream of debris left behind by comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, which orbits the sun approximately every 33 years.

As tiny particles of comet dust enter Earth's atmosphere at speeds of around 44 miles (71 kilometers) per second, they burn up and produce brilliant streaks of light we know as meteors, or shooting stars.

Most years, the Leonids produce relatively modest displays with around 10 to 15 meteors per hour under ideal viewing conditions. But occasionally, Earth encounters a particularly dense trail of debris, triggering a meteor storm.

Will we ever see another meteor storm like 1966?

The Leonids have a long history of putting on some spectacular displays, with significant storms recorded in 1833 and 1866. And 1966 wasn't the last time the Leonids put on an extraordinary show. In 1999, 2001 and 2002, the Leonids once again reached meteor-storm levels, producing thousands of meteors per hour at their peaks. The shows aren't over yet! With comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle due to return in 2031, astronomers are already looking ahead to what the following years could bring.

A study released in August 2026 predicts potentially impressive Leonid displays in 2033 and 2034, with peak rates exceeding 1,000 meteors per hour. However, these forecasts remain uncertain, and a repeat of the extraordinary 1966 storm is far from guaranteed.

For now, we'll just have to wait and see.

]]> <![CDATA[ Satellites now outnumber the visible stars above most towns ]]> More than 700 satellites are crossing the sky over an average mid-latitude town at any moment of the night, outnumbering in many cases the stars visible to the naked eye.

That's based on an analysis of the trajectories of the 15,833 active satellites that currently circle the planet in low Earth orbit below an altitude of 1,200 miles (2,000 kilometers). Analyzing data from Oct. 12 and 18 this year, researchers found that with a completely unobstructed horizon, 710 satellites were crossing the sky in every single moment of the night above an average U.K. town.

The results were published as a non-peer-reviewed study conducted by engineering firm Accu Components, and is based on satellite monitoring data from the U.S. Space Force available through the public website CelesTrak. Although the researchers specifically focused on the U.K., they say that such heavy satellite traffic flows above most of Europe, the U.S. and other mid-latitude regions, especially between 40 and 50 degrees north or south.

"Most Starlink satellites orbit at around 53 degrees to the equator, so the satellites bunch up over the mid-latitudes. These worldwide figures are approximate, based on a global grid over a single day," Accu Components spokesperson told Space.com in an email. "Skies near the equator are the quietest, with around 490 satellites."

Not all of those satellites are visible to the naked eye, the researchers said in a statement. Because satellites unlike stars don't produce their own light, they must be illuminated by the sun, while the ground below has already sunk into darkness, to be visible. According to the study, an average of 105 satellites out of those 710 were catching light as they zoomed overhead, shining as bright as stars.

The spokesperson said that the actual number of visible satellites varies drastically throughout the night. During the hours after dusk and before dawn, a much greater number of satellites can be seen, while in the middle of the night most no longer catch any light.

"For a typical U.K. town, around 300 satellites are catching the sunlight in the first hour or so after dark," the spokesperson said. "That falls to fewer than 20 around midnight, then climbs back to around 300 before dawn."

For comparison, as little as a few dozen stars are visible to the naked eye in the dead of the night above large, light-polluted megalopolis such as London or New York, according to OwnStarMap. In suburban areas and smaller towns, that number grows to a few hundred. To get to a few thousand visible stars, one must retreat into remote countryside or isolated mountain ranges.

The number of satellites orbiting Earth has grown steeply in the past decade, especially since Elon Musk’s SpaceX began launching its internet-beaming Starlink constellation. Satellite companies plan to launch hundreds of thousands, possibly millions of satellites in the coming decades. If those visions come to pass, the number of passing satellites will vastly outgrow that of stars almost anywhere in the world. The trend especially concerns astronomers who fear the impacts on humankind’s ability to study the Universe.

Satellites crossing the view of ground-based telescopes leave streaks in astronomical images and increase the overall brightness of the sky through the light they reflect down towards Earth. Gradually, even the most powerful telescopes could lose their ability to see the distant stars and galaxies that hold the answers to key questions about the history of the universe.

The study found that throughout the night, an average U.K. town sees 12,891 different satellites passing overhead.

]]> <![CDATA[ On this day in space! Nov. 16, 1974: The giant Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico broadcasts humanity's 1st interstellar message ]]>

On Nov. 16, 1974, humans sent their first message to the stars in an attempt to contact extraterrestrials.

They did this using what was then the largest radio telescope in the world, located at the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico. A group of scientists led by Frank Drake and Carl Sagan sent their message to the M13 star cluster. The message was written in binary code and contained information about human DNA.

It also included figures of a human, the solar system and the Arecibo telescope. The idea was that if any aliens were to receive the signal and figure out how to decode it, they would know where it came from. Because M13 is 25,000 light-years away, it will take 25,000 years for any M13 aliens to hear our message — if they are even out there.

Why it mattered

The Arecibo message is only one of several messages intended for extraterrestrials, but this signal sent from Puerto Rico in 1974 was humanity's first intentional olive branch to the stars. At the time, it was the most powerful broadcast ever beamed into space, according to the SETI Institute.

"The broadcast was particularly powerful because it used Arecibo's megawatt transmitter attached to its 305 meter antenna," SETI wrote of the broadcast in a project over. "The emission was equivalent to a 20 trillion watt omnidirectional broadcast, and would be detectable by a SETI experiment just about anywhere in the galaxy, assuming a receiving antenna similar in size to Arecibo's."

The message was designed by astronomy professor Frank Drake of Cornell University (who also developed the famed Drake Equation for alien life), as well as Cornnell graduate students Richard Isaacman and Linda May, and Arecibo staff member James Walker, with input from astronomer Carl Sagan and others, according to Cornell University.

The message included 1,679 bits that were arranged in 73 lines of 23 characters per line, all prime numbers, with the broadcast lasting less than 3 minutes, according to SETI.

As of 2026, the message should have traveled about 52 light-years (1 light-year is the distance light travels in a year), with 24,948 light-years to go before reaching star cluster M13.

The Arecibo message may have been the first message of its kind, but it wasn't the last. We have also included messages on several spacecraft, such as Pioneer and Voyager. NASA and Paul McCartney also beamed a performance of "Across the Universe" in 2008.

Here's what Voyager 1's latest milestone means for the interstellar probe ]]> After nearly 50 years traveling through space, NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft is approaching a milestone no human-made object has reached before: a distance of one light-day from Earth.

This milestone — which Voyager 1 is expected to reach on Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026, at 5:16:07 a.m. EST (1016:07 GMT) — highlights the immense distances Voyager 1 has traveled and the challenges of communicating with spacecraft operating in the outer reaches of the solar system and beyond.

Astronomers use a measurement known as a light-day to describe how far light travels in 24 hours. Light moves at approximately 186,000 miles (300,000 kilometers) per second, meaning one light-day is roughly 16 billion miles (about 26 billion kilometers), according to a statement from NASA.

Although the term light-day might sound like a measurement of time, it is actually a unit of distance, much like a light-year. Astronomers use light-based measurements because conventional miles and kilometers become increasingly difficult to comprehend when describing the enormous distances between objects in space.

For perspective on how far Voyager 1 has travelled, sunlight takes about eight minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth, meaning our planet is approximately 8.3 light-minutes from the sun. Radio signals traveling between Earth and Mars can take anywhere from three to 22 minutes, depending on the planets' positions in their orbits, according to the statement.

By comparison, when Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth, a radio signal sent from the probe will take a full 24 hours to reach mission controllers on Earth, and a command transmitted from Earth will take another 24 hours to reach the spacecraft.

The communication delay affects how engineers operate spacecraft at such distances. Unlike spacecraft operating closer to Earth, which can receive commands and return data with relatively little delay, communicating with Voyager 1 requires mission controllers to account for the extended signal travel time when planning spacecraft operations, troubleshooting technical issues and evaluating the results of commands sent to the probe.

Voyager 1 has been traveling away from Earth since its launch on Sept. 5, 1977. Now cruising through interstellar space at nearly 38,000 mph (61,000 kph), the spacecraft has spent more than 49 years covering the distance that light can cross in a single day.

Even at that speed, Voyager 1 is moving relatively slowly compared with light itself. Its twin, Voyager 2, which launched in 1977 on a different trajectory, is expected to reach the same one-light-day milestone in November 2035.

As Voyager 1 and, eventually, Voyager 2 continue their journeys through interstellar space, their growing distances from Earth offer a measure of both the reach of human exploration and the communication challenges that come with sending spacecraft ever farther into the cosmos.

"We decided, as a parental unit, Dionna and I, that we were going to put as much effort into making sure our family was ready as NASA was putting into making sure I was ready to be a crew member," Glover explained.

The family visited NASA's Kennedy Space Center, toured the launch pad and crew quarters and even planned when Glover would call home from the International Space Station. But by the time Artemis II came around, things were different. All four of his daughters were now adults, and preparing them for his journey around the moon meant discussing the mission's risks, including the possibility that he might not return home.

Glover recalled his wife telling him something he described as maybe the scariest thing he'd ever heard.

"You should have this talk with our daughters."

And although he knew she was right, it wasn't an easy conversation to have.

"We did, and it did not go well in my opinion," Glover admitted. "Well, it's not about going well. The talk needed to be done, just because it's hard."

The following day, Glover sent his daughters and wife a poem, Live Your Life, by Chief Tecumseh.

The poem helped Glover express something he had struggled to put into words during their conversation: why he believed the risks of traveling to the moon were worth taking.

"It was a very tough conversation, but they understood that I know this is risky. I wasn't just telling them Dad's risking his life. There's a real point to this and there's a reason to take this risk," Glover explained. "This poem helped me to say it in a way that I didn't have words for."

"Splashdown."

"It's the true, ultimate mission accomplishment. Just 'we did it.' We survived. My family is relieved, and there's just nothing like it," Glover explained. "There's nothing like coming home. There's nothing like returning to Earth."

]]> <![CDATA[ The Leonid meteor shower peaks tonight! Here's what you need to know ]]> The Leonid meteor shower peaks tonight (Nov. 17-18) sending shooting stars and fireballs across the autumn sky as Earth passes through a stream of debris left by Comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle.

Up to 15 meteors could be spotted per hour under perfect dark sky conditions on the night of Nov. 17-18, according to the International Meteor Organisation. NASA, meanwhile, has given a more conservative rate of less than three meteors per hour — time will tell.

Leonid meteors appear to race away from a point of origin, or radiant, in the constellation Leo, which glistens high above the southeastern horizon in the hours before dawn in mid-November. Both Jupiter and Mars will be separated by just a few degrees in the constellation Leo on the night of the peak, making it particularly easy to find in 2026!

When is the best time to look for Leonid meteors?

The best time to spot Leonids is in the hours before dawn on Nov. 18, when the radiant will reach its highest point in the southeastern sky, maximizing the amount of meteors that may be seen skimming through Earth's atmosphere. By then, the waxing moon will have set, leaving darker skies and a better chance of spotting fainter meteors.

Shooting stars that appear close to the radiant will strike Earth almost head-on, leaving the shortest trails. Instead, find a patch of sky a short distance away from the constellation Leo, where the meteors will be at their most impressive, and give your eyes 20-30 minutes to fully adapt to the dark.

Why are the Leonids special?

As if shooting stars weren't enough, the Leonid shower is also known for spawning dazzling fireballs and long-lasting Earth-grazing meteors, which strike our atmosphere at an oblique angle, leaving long trains as they skim through before passing back out into space.

The shower is also capable of producing magnificent meteor storms when Earth passes through particularly dense trails of debris left behind by Comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, which orbits the sun approximately every 33 years.

 <description>Od událostí 17. listopadu 1989 uplynulo 37 let. Co zůstalo z tehdejších ideálů a euforie? Co charakterizuje polistopadovou demokracii a nakolik jsme spokojeni s jejím fungováním? Jaká je naše vize budoucnosti? A co do ulic přivádí dnešní mladou generaci? Nejen o tom přišli diskutovat spisovatelka Pavla Horáková, historik Jiří Suk a sociolog Martin Buchtík. Na dálku do debaty přispěla greenfluencerka a studentka Rozárie Haškovcová.</description>

 <description>Jeden za svobodu bojoval, druhá se snaží odkaz sametové revoluce předat mladé generaci. Signatář Charty 77 Miroslav Lehký a ředitelka organizace Díky, že můžem Bára Stárek se na Národní třídě zamýšleli nad významem 17. listopadu. „Nepředpokládal jsem, že po tolika letech zůstane listopad 1989 v myslích a srdcích lidí,“ přiznává Lehký. „Je to náš nejmodernější státní svátek, který si naše společnost nejvíc pamatuje,“ tvrdí Stárek.</description>

   <description>Zdražování elektroniky už není jen problémem počítačových nadšenců, kteří si kupují operační paměti nebo výkonné grafické karty. Podle analytiků a technologických společností se situace nemusí zlepšit ani v příštím roce. Vyplatí se tedy letošní slevy na Black Friday, nebo je lepší nákupy odložit?       <title>NATO chce obnovit systém Starshield, Ukrajina však stále bojuje s výpadky</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni/valka-na-ukrajine-starshield-ukrajina-zelenskyj.A261117_155204_zahranicni_aya#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Generální tajemník NATO Mark Rutte v úterý uvedl, že příslušné strany pracují na tom, aby byl satelitní systém Starshield, který Ukrajina využívá ke komunikaci na bojišti, co nejdříve opět plně funkční. Ukrajinský prezident Volodymyr Zelenskyj ve čtvrtek upozornil, že ukrajinská armáda zaznamenává již několik dní výrazné výpadky systému Starshield společnosti Elona Muska. Problémy se podle něj týkají celé frontové linie i částí Ukrajiny okupovaných Ruskem.

 <description>Ukrajinská armáda v noci na úterý podnikla operaci, při které zasáhla Krymský most, jenž spojuje poloostrov s ruskou pevninou. Na základě hodnocení dostupných fotografií a videí vyplývá, že byl most poškozen a část konstrukce se zřítila do moře. Moskva rozsah škod neupřesnila, ale uvedla, že doprava na mostě byla zastavena.  <description>Slovenská vláda v úterý 17. listopadu projednala výsledky říjnové schůzky členů mezivládní slovensko-ruské komise v Moskvě. Ministr zahraničí Juraj Blanár po skončení jednání obhajoval kontakty Bratislavy s Ruskem v době jeho pokračující vojenské invaze na Ukrajině. <item>
 <title>Papež Lev XVI. neplánuje povolit kněžím svatbu. Nevyloučil ale, že jednou duchovními budou i ženatí</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/papez-lev-xvi-neplanuje-povolit-knezim-svatbu-nevyloucil-ale-ze-jednou_2611171218_cen</link>
 <description>Papež Lev XIV. v úterý řekl, že v současné době neplánuje změnit katolické učení tak, aby umožňovalo kněžství ženatých mužů. Podle něj to vyvolává příliš velké rozpory v církvi, informovala agentura Reuters. Hlava katolické církve se tak poprvé vyjádřila k návrhu, který už dlouho podporuje řada katolíků, a to na palubě papežského speciálu vracejícího se z Peru do Říma.</description>

 <description>Záhadný protestní transparent a pátrání, které dostalo nečekané rozuzlení. V Bratislavě si sametovou revoluci připomínají i exponátem, který ještě loni ležel po demonstraci na ulici. Městské muzeum ho vystavilo, ale neznalo jeho autora. Rozhodlo se proto vyhlásit pátrání. A odpověď přišla v okamžiku, kdy ji nikdo nečekal.</description>

 <description>Slovensko kvůli výhrůžnému e-mailu omezilo vlakovou dopravu na hlavním koridoru na západě země. Policie vyslala jednotky k pyrotechnickým prohlídkám, situaci ale nevyhodnotila jako vysoký stupeň ohrožení. Informovala o tom slovenská média. Vlaky kvůli nařízenému zpomalení rychlosti jízdy nabraly zpoždění, podle odborného webu je důvodem omezení nahlášení výbušného systému.</description>

 <title>Turecké úřady provedly razii v další opoziční televizi. Do vedení stanice Sözcü TV dosadily svého správce</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/turecke-urady-provedly-razii-v-dalsi-opozicni-televizi-do-vedeni-stanice-sozcu_2611171028_cen</link>
 <description>Turecké úřady před svítáním provedly razii v sídle jedné z posledních velkých televizních stanic spojených s opozicí, zadržely několik vedoucích pracovníků a jmenovaly správce, který bude řídit její provoz. <item>
 <title>AfD nabízí čokoládového Mikuláše držícího knihu s logem strany. Překročení hranic, zní z církve</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/afd-nabizi-cokoladoveho-mikulase-drziciho-knihu-s-logem-strany-prekroceni-hranic_2611170739_bod</link>
 <description>Alternativa pro Německo (AfD) ve svém internetovém obchodě nabízí čokoládové figurky svatého Mikuláše, které pod paží drží knihu s logem této protiimigrační strany. Nelíbí se to essenskému biskupovi Franzi-Josefu Overbeckovi, napsal bulvární server Bild.de.</description>

<item>
 <title>ONLINE: Část Krymského mostu se nejspíše zřítila do moře, vyplývá z fotografií a videí</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/online-ruske-sily-znicily-na-800-ukrajinskych-dronu-mirily-na-moskvu-rakety-v_2611170634_jho</link>
 <description>Jedna ze silničních částí Krymského mostu se včetně oblouku po nočním ukrajinském zásahu zřítila do moře. Tvrdí to telegramový kanál Exilenova+ s tím, že to vyplývá z hodnocení dostupných fotografií a videí. Rusko, které ukrajinský autonomní poloostrov Krym okupuje, o ukrajinském úderu na most informovalo, rozsah škod ale neupřesnilo. Agentura TASS pouze uvedla, že doprava na mostě byla zastavena.</description>

O tom, co se děje, se první Liberečáci dozvěděli až o den později.</description></item><item><title>Stavbou roku 2026 je i krajská náplavka v Liberci</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905982-stavbou-roku-2026-je-i-krajska-naplavka-v-liberci.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905982-stavbou-roku-2026-je-i-krajska-naplavka-v-liberci.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:00:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Také náplavka u sídla Libereckého kraje se stal Stavbou roku 2026. Ocenění získalo včera 15 projektů v ČR, například modernizace trati a výstavba nádražní budovy Praha-Bubny či rekonstrukce stanice metra Českomoravská. Ocenění získala náplavka bez jednoho dne přesně rok po svém otevření.</description></item><item><title>Ježíškova vnoučata opět plní sny. V Libereckém kraji čeká na dárce na 150 seniorů</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905928-jeziskova-vnoucata-opet-plni-sny-v-libereckem-kraji-ceka-na-darce-na-150-senioru.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905928-jeziskova-vnoucata-opet-plni-sny-v-libereckem-kraji-ceka-na-darce-na-150-senioru.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:33:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Zimní bundu či boty, model vláčku, projížďku koňským spřežením i vyzkoušet letecký simulátor si letos přejí osamělí senioři v Libereckém kraji. Jejich přání si lidé mohou rezervovat a splnit v jubilejním 10. ročníku projektu Ježíškova vnoučata, který včera odstartoval na webu jeziskovavnoucata.cz.</description></item><item><title>Záchranář Vláďa shání peníze na defibrilátor pro záchranu životů i mimo službu</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905906-zachranar-vlada-shani-penize-na-defibrilator-pro-zachranu-zivotu-i-mimo-sluzbu.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905906-zachranar-vlada-shani-penize-na-defibrilator-pro-zachranu-zivotu-i-mimo-sluzbu.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 06:40:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Více než dvacet let zachraňuje životy jako profesionál u záchranné služby Libereckého kraje, pomáhá ale i na cestách nebo jako dobrovolný First Responder. Záchranář Vladimír Gudas Sýs teď prosí veřejnost o pomoc ve sbírce na Donio. Vybrané peníze mu pomohou koupit vlastní automatický defibrilátor.</description></item><item><title>Česká Lípa má nového starostu. Jakub Mencl vystřídal Jitku Volfovou</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/905964-ceska-lipa-ma-noveho-starostu-jakub-mencl-vystridal-jitku-volfovou.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/905964-ceska-lipa-ma-noveho-starostu-jakub-mencl-vystridal-jitku-volfovou.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 19:45:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Politika</category><description>Česká Lípa má oficiálně osmého porevolučního starostu. Po dvaadvaceti letech navíc jde o muže. Nově bude starostovat Jakub Mencl (Živá Lípa), který vystřídal Jitku Volfovou (ANO), která byla starostkou poslední dvě volební období.</description></item><item><title>Vážná nehoda u Pertoltic. Mladá řidička předjížděla přes plnou čáru</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/905959-vazna-nehoda-u-pertoltic-mlada-ridicka-predjizdela-pres-plnou-caru.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/905959-vazna-nehoda-u-pertoltic-mlada-ridicka-predjizdela-pres-plnou-caru.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 18:39:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Krimi</category><description>Středně těžké poranění si vyžádala dopravní nehoda, ke které došlo v pondělí před polednem v katastru Pertoltic. Mladá řidička na silnici 270 mezi Jablonným a Mimoní předjížděla na úseku s plnou čárou a auto několikrát přetočila přes střechu.</description></item><item><title>V úterý je svátek. Jak to bude 17. listopadu s nákupy?</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905875-zitra-je-svatek-jak-to-bude-17-listopadu-s-nakupy.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905875-zitra-je-svatek-jak-to-bude-17-listopadu-s-nakupy.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 17:45:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Markéta Hamerníková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Úterní státní svátek přináší i praktickou otázku: bude kde nakoupit? Zatímco 28. října musely velké prodejny zavřít, pro úterý 17. listopadu platí jiná pravidla. Rozhodující není samotný svátek, ale to, zda ho zákon zahrnuje mezi dny se zákazem prodeje.</description></item><item><title>Liberec dnes zahájil provoz první linky poptávkové dopravy</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/905901-liberec-dnes-zahajil-provoz-prvni-linky-poptavkove-dopravy.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/905901-liberec-dnes-zahajil-provoz-prvni-linky-poptavkove-dopravy.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:00:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Doprava</category><description>Dopravní podnik v Liberci (DPMLJ) dnes zahájil provoz první linky poptávkové dopravy, kdy vozidlo MHD přijede na objednání. Službu zavedl v Pilínkově pro Puškinovu ulici a okolí, odkud to mají někteří obyvatelé k nejbližší zastávce MHD tři čtvrtě hodiny chůze.</description></item></channel></rss>

výběžek.eu https://www.vybezek.eu dobrý den ze šluknovského výběžku, konce světa - šluknovský výběžek Mon, 16 Nov 2026 14:12:33 +0000 cs hourly 1 https://wordpress.org/?v=7.1.4 https://www.vybezek.eu/wp-uploads/2018/09/cropped-favicon-vybezek-32x32.png výběžek.eu https://www.vybezek.eu 32 32 Starostovník 2026 https://www.vybezek.eu/295747-starostovnik-2026/ Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:41:02 +0000 https://www.vybezek.eu/?p=295747 V termínu 9. a 10. října 2026 proběhly další komunální (a senátní) volby, Tudíž je čas na aktualizaci – snad už mají všichni na svých webech všechno správně.

Vlastně je to obdivuhodné (nebo spíš pozoruhodné?). Někde vážně stačí postavit jednu jedinou kandidátku a všechno je OK. Někde ostřílení matadoři zmizeli v propadlišti dějin a došlo k totální proměně. Někde opakují stále stejné chyby. Ale hlavně – pořád zůstává faktem, že spousta nespokojených a nadávajících nedokáže zvednout pozadí a zkusit cokoli dělat. Víte, že aby místní referendum bylo platné, musí se jej zúčastnit alespoň 35 %?

Dolní Podluží –

Dolní Podluží na FB:

DOLNÍ PODLUŽÍ MÁ NOVÉ VEDENÍ OBCE
Dnes proběhlo ustavující zasedání Zastupitelstva obce Dolní Podluží pro volební období 2026–2030.
Starostou obce byl zvolen pan Vít Nesnídal a místostarostou pan Jan Hampl.
Nově zvolenému vedení obce i všem členům zastupitelstva přejeme mnoho úspěchů, vzájemné spolupráce a správných rozhodnutí ve prospěch naší obce a jejích obyvatel.
Ať se Dolnímu Podluží daří i v dalších letech!

Město Jiříkov na FB:

NOVÉ ZASTUPITELSTVO JIŘÍKOVA ZAHÁJILO SVÉ VOLEBNÍ OBDOBÍ
(Jiříkovské noviny listopad 2026)
V pondělí 9. 11. 2026 se uskutečnilo ustavující zasedání Zastupitelstva města Jiříkov, které zahájilo nové čtyřleté volební období 2026–2030. Na programu bylo především složení slibu nově zvolených zastupitelů, volba vedení města a dalších orgánů samosprávy.

Život jde dál:

Varnsdorfský minitrh? Za nás rozhodně povedená sobota!

Včera jsme vyrazili do Městské knihovny ve Varnsdorfu a rozhodně jsme tam nebyli jen do počtu! Roman představil svou už třetí pohádkovou knížku Mokré pohádky a my jsme s sebou přivezli také kousek našeho Život jde dál. Výrobky, na kterých se podíleli nevidomí a slabozrací, spoustu věcí k vidění i k zakoupení a hlavně chuť potkávat se s lidmi.

A že se jich u nás zastavilo! Někdo nakoupil, někdo si přišel popovídat, někdo nás podpořil jen svou přítomností. A přesně o tom to je. Každá taková podpora se počítá a každé milé setkání potěší.

Obrovské díky naší babče, Vlaďce Hermanové a Renatě Šimákové, které nám s tím vším pomáhaly. A samozřejmě děkujeme paní ředitelce za pozvání, milé přijetí a atmosféru, ve které se člověk cítí jako mezi svými.

Děkujeme všem, kteří za námi přišli, podpořili nás a udělali si čas. Bylo nám s vámi krásně!

Život jde dál a my jsme rádi, že jdete s námi.

Visit Varnsdorf:

Náš kraj má co vyprávět. A Regionální knižní minitrh to znovu potvrdil.

Za každou knihou je příběh. Za každým rukodělným výrobkem hodiny práce, nápadů a šikovných rukou. A za každou uchovanou tradicí člověk, kterému záleží na tom, aby nezmizela.

Právě takové bylo sobotní setkání s lidmi, kteří mají co říct, co předat a především chuť tvořit. S autory, kteří vydávají knihy a uchovávají příběhy našeho regionu. S tvůrci a řemeslníky, kteří vlastníma rukama vyrábějí originální věci, navazují na tradice a dávají jim nový život. Právě jejich práce, nápady a nadšení pomáhají udržovat místní kulturu živou a připomínají, jak bohatý a inspirativní náš kraj je.

Velké poděkování patří všem, kteří se na minitrhu představili. Ať už prostřednictvím svých knih, rukodělných výrobků, poctivé řemeslné práce nebo osobního příběhu. Děkujeme, že svou tvorbou obohacujete náš region a pomáháte uchovávat jeho jedinečnost pro další generace.
